validity.recommendation: Flag for dedup review against P1865 (Tripoli-Mellitah, 158km), P1864 (Khoms-Tripoli, 201km), P1863 (Brega-Khoms, 645km) and P1862 (Brega-Benghazi, 396km) — decide whether P0483 should be a non-summed network-grouping label (excluded from aggregate length/capacity totals) or merged/retired so the corridor isn't double-counted.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed real and correctly classified. The sheet's own two citations: (1) a Facebook photo link — 200 live but no extractable text, useless as a spec source (not cited); (2) a World Bank/Tractebel Engineering report 'Fuel Availability & Opportunities for Cost Reduction Report' (Libya: Supporting Electricity Sector Reform, 18 Dec 2017) — verified live (200) via WebFetch + manual pdftotext extraction (url_verifier's automated substring screen false-negatived on this PDF per its own documented PDF-extraction caveat; I confirmed the exact phrases manually). This report independently and repeatedly describes a '34" Coastal Pipeline system with a total longitude of ~1,120 km' connecting Libya's West and East gas network areas via Mellitah (West Entry Point) -> Marsa El Brega -> Benghazi (East Entry Point) — matching GEM's recorded endpoints (Mellitah Complex->Benghazi), diameter (34in, exact match) and length (1164km vs source's ~1120km, ~4% high, within normal rounding tolerance). Status=operating and Fuel=Gas are both well-supported by extensive context (flows, injection, consumption figures) even though the literal word 'operating' isn't required per the confidence-tier rules. Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp' 100% is plausible: the source states NOC 'is in charge of exploration, production, transportation and commercialization of O&G' and that a NOC subsidiary, General Gas Transmission and Distribution Company (GGT&D, est. 2007), specifically 'construct[s] and manage[s]' the gas distribution/transmission network — so GGT&D may be the more precise operator/owner-of-record than the parent NOC, but NOC as ultimate state owner is not wrong. DUPLICATE CONCERN: the same World Bank source explicitly decomposes this 'Coastal Pipeline' into constituent legs that GEM ALSO tracks as separate ProjectIDs on the in-scope roster: the western leg (871km total) splits into a Mellitah->Tripoli->Khoms trench (222km, ~600 mmscf/d nominal) and a Brega->Khoms trench (645km, ~370 mmscf/d) — the latter length matches P1863 'Brega-Khoms Gas Pipeline' (645km) almost exactly; and the eastern leg is Marsa El Brega->Benghazi (246km, ~410 mmscf/d), the same route as P1862 'Brega-Benghazi Gas Pipeline' (though P1862's recorded length of 396km diverges from the source's 246km for that same leg — a separate P1862 issue, out of scope here but worth flagging to whoever re-audits P1862). P1865 'Tripoli-Mellitah' (158km) and P1864 'Khoms-Tripoli' (201km) together (359km) roughly correspond to the source's single 222km Mellitah-Tripoli-Khoms trench, again not a clean 1:1 match but clearly the same physical corridor split differently. Net effect: GEM appears to carry BOTH a system/network-level 'Coastal Pipeline' entity (P0483, cluster/rollup framing, len 1164/cap 604) AND its physical constituent segments as separate full-attribute rows (P1865/P1864/P1863/P1862) — this is the exact 'dual-level granularity' pattern this project's own reconciliation SOP acknowledges (network-grouping rows vs individual segment rows) and it risks double-counting length/capacity if both are summed in aggregate tracker statistics. This is a structural/dedup issue, not a fabrication — recommend NOT silently deleting either level, but flagging for a maintainer decision on which layer carries the aggregate totals.

validity.recommendation: Leave Capacity sourced but flag as approximate/unconfirmed — no independent source gives a single 604 MMcf/d end-to-end figure; also flag StartYear1=1983 as unconfirmed.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records a single Capacity=604.00 MMcf/d for the whole Mellitah->Benghazi corridor. The one strong independent source I could verify (World Bank/Tractebel 2017 report, same doc used above) gives THREE DIFFERENT segment-level nominal capacities for this same corridor rather than one system-wide number: ~600 mmscf/d (Mellitah->Tripoli->Khoms trench), ~370 mmscf/d (Brega->Khoms trench), and ~410 mmscf/d (Brega->Benghazi eastern leg). None of these equals 604, and a true through-line bottleneck capacity for a corridor built from unequal segments would logically be capped near the lowest segment (~370 mmscf/d), not 604 — so 604 looks like it may conflate/round the western Mellitah-Khoms trench figure (~600) rather than represent genuine end-to-end throughput. This is a material disagreement per the sweep's own rule ('mentions the pipeline' is not enough — the source must agree with the GEM number), so I'm not passing Capacity as confirmed. Separately, the sheet's StartYear1=1983: I found no source (this report or otherwise) corroborating a 1983 construction/inauguration date for this pipeline specifically — the report's only nearby '1983' reference is the unrelated Tobruk power STATION commissioning date, which is plausibly where a wrong 1983 could have been transcribed from if that ever happened, though I have no direct evidence of that mix-up, only that 1983 is unconfirmed as-is. Recommend Baird's team keep both fields but treat them as unverified rather than sourced.

summary: Real, correctly-classified corridor (34in Mellitah-Brega-Benghazi 'Coastal Pipeline', ~1120km per World Bank/Tractebel 2017 report vs GEM's 1164km) but likely double-counted: its length/capacity overlap with already-tracked segments P1865, P1864, P1863 and P1862 (duplicate concern); separately, GEM's single 604 MMcf/d capacity figure conflicts with the same source's per-segment capacities (370/410/600 mmscf/d) and StartYear1=1983 is unconfirmed (spec concern).
